lead: The network started with 11 masts and a spreadsheet. The full history is in the institute's 20th anniversary report.

entries.title: 11 stations go live
entries.text: The first masts are installed between Talhof and the weir. They are funded for three years and meant to be removed afterwards.

entries.title: The series becomes public
entries.text: Readings move from an internal spreadsheet to an open portal. Within a month, a secondary school uses them in class.

entries.title: 46 masts and a full winter without gaps
entries.text: Local storage on every station closes the gaps that had made January data unusable for five years.

entries.title: Raw and checked data published side by side
entries.text: It was not a popular decision inside the institute. It is now the main reason external users say they trust the checked data.

entries.title: The refit
entries.text: One specification for every mast, so a failed part can be swapped from a van instead of ordered.

entries.title: The warmest summer on record
entries.text: Three shallow stations stayed above 21 degrees for 11 days in a row. The network was now dense enough to show where the warming started.
